evidence.section: Adventuring in the Dwarf Realms / On the Road
evidence.claim: Dwarf roadbuilding and trade travel support the target category. The account describes specific ancient roads; their provenance, material and historical importance are not properties of a generated DF road.

evidence.section: The Dwarf Kingdoms / On the Road continued
evidence.claim: Mountain travel and guarded roadside infrastructure provide the context for landscape and watchtower images. Selecting an image is a Forthammer adaptation, not evidence that the named DF road reaches that landmark.
Context selects the documented colour senses, not metal composition or blood. Compounds are new labels using source words; no complete road-naming grammar is claimed.
Ungdrin denotes the Underway, not an unrestricted generic road. It is excluded to avoid inventing an ancient road connection or applying an underground word to an ordinary road.

evidence.section: Dawn of a New Age context (printed p14 / PDF p17)
evidence.quote: the Dwarfs established new trade routes
evidence.claim: The army book corroborates Dwarf roadbuilding and trade routes. Generated names do not inherit these routes, their builders or their history.

evidence.section: The Cult of Handrich / Wavemaster Sullandiel Fartrader
evidence.quote: He served as ambassador to Karaz Bryn
evidence.claim: Karaz Bryn is an established location, identified as the Silver Pinnacle in Josh Reynolds, Neferata. Native head-first generation must not reuse it; the reversed compact proposal Brynkaraz is separately evaluated.

evidence.section: The Great Council, battle account before The Winter of Woe
evidence.claim: Karaz-Zan is an attested historical battle name. Exclude the normalized name from native road generation; no generated road inherits that event.
Bar supplies a gateway emblem in the existing context of guarded road travel. It does not identify a real gate, claim a defended border, confer ownership, or establish a route destination.
Kadrin supplies a mountain-pass emblem, supported by the road-travel context on p19. This is a symbolic label, not a surveyed route through an actual pass or a safety guarantee.

evidence.section: Khazalid Glossary: Stromez, Varn, Zorn, Zon
evidence.claim: Zorn selects the upland-plateau sense. Stromez, Varn and Zon supply stream, mountain lake and sun. Their use as emblems is a composition, not an assertion of real surrounding geography, destination, direction, sunlight, a solar naming custom, or sacred status.
The glossary distinguishes a musical horn from horn material, and attests road and thunder. Selected nouns remain literal word senses inside adapted labels.
The selected moonlight sense and the printed material, shadow, work and sunrise nouns add distinct concepts. No generic machine, dawn-direction, geology or ancestry meaning is invented.

The conjunction explicitly pairs two reviewed images. Thrag means wound, Thrynaz includes laws, Tiwaz includes rest and Skaud includes song. These are not new translations for hospital, government or tavern.

High-resolution printed text confirms Zunthrum with n. Spear, money, sunset, remembering and gift are independently attested; none assigns actual stock, wealth, a historical event or a commemorated person.
